concept.title: Symmetric Colorings of Hales-Jewett Cubes Coincide with One-Weight Colorings
concept.concept_description: Every symmetric r-coloring of the Hales-Jewett cube [t]^n — one invariant under all coordinate permutations of the word — is a one-weight coloring: there exist integer weights w_1, ..., w_t such that the color of a word x ∈ [t]^n depends only on the weighted sum ∑_i w_{x_i}. Conversely, every one-weight coloring is symmetric. This equivalence reduces the symmetric lower-bound problem for Hales-Jewett numbers to the d=1 case of Gallai's theorem on homothetic copies of a t-point set in Z.

For the converse, given a symmetric coloring c, construct the radix weight by examining how c distinguishes words that differ only in letter substitution: define w_j - w_1 as the minimal coordinate substitution that changes the color class when swapping a letter 1 for letter j in a fixed position. Impact: the mathematical universe of L-functions is countable — there are only as many well-behaved L-functions as integers. and `|y|`.  This turns the two diagonals `y = x` and `y = −x` into a genuine

noncomputable def sech (t : ℝ) : ℝ := 1 / Real.cosh t

noncomputable def splitCurv (x y : ℝ) : ℝ := (sech x) ^ 2 - (sech y) ^ 2

/-- First diagonal coefficient of the split metric `ds² = E · dx² + G · dy²`. -/
noncomputable def metricE (y : ℝ) : ℝ := (sech y) ^ 2

/-- Second diagonal coefficient of the split metric `ds² = E · dx² + G · dy²`. -/
noncomputable def metricG (x : ℝ) : ℝ := (Real.cosh x) ^ 2

lemma sech_pos (t : ℝ) : 0 < sech t := by
  unfold sech; positivity

lemma sech_le_one (t : ℝ) : sech t ≤ 1 := by
  unfold sech
  rw [div_le_one (cosh_pos t)]
  exact one_le_cosh t

lemma sq_sech_lt_iff (x y : ℝ) :

  simp only [sech, one_div, inv_pow]
  rw [inv_lt_inv₀ (by positivity) (by positivity)]
  constructor
  · intro h; nlinarith [cosh_pos x, cosh_pos y]
  · intro h; nlinarith [cosh_pos x, cosh_pos y]

lemma splitCurv_antisymm (x y : ℝ) : splitCurv x y = - splitCurv y x := by
  unfold splitCurv; ring

/-- Flatness on the main diagonal `y = x`. -/
lemma splitCurv_diag (x : ℝ) : splitCurv x x = 0 := by
  unfold splitCurv; ring

/-- Flatness on the anti-diagonal `y = -x`. -/
lemma splitCurv_antidiag (x : ℝ) : splitCurv x (-x) = 0 := by
  unfold splitCurv sech; rw [cosh_neg]; ring

  simp only [splitCurv, sech, sub_eq_zero, one_div, inv_pow, inv_inj]

  · intro h

  rw [sub_pos, sq_sech_lt_iff, cosh_lt_cosh]
